awd_titl_txt: Conference: The 19th US-Korea Forum on Nanotechnology: Neuromorphic & Quantum Sensors on a Chip and Sustainability in Semiconductor Manufacturing by Design
awd_abstract_narration:
Nontechnical Description:
Nanotechnology plays a critical role in fueling advances in information technology. Miniaturization and scaling of the basic devices that underpin all leading technologies in computing, communication, and sensing are based on innovations, and therefore research advances, in nanotechnology.  This project will support the 19th Nanotechnology Forum between the United States and South Korea, which will be held July 3-4, 2025, in Kintex, Gyeonggi-do, South Korea. Past nanotechnology fora between the two countries have addressed leading-edge topics at the time of each forum. The present forum will continue this tradition by focusing on nanotechnology issues related to Neuromorphic Computing, Quantum Sensing, and Sustainability in Semiconductor Manufacturing by Design. The key objective of past fora, including this one, is to facilitate networking among members of the research communities and funding agencies of the two countries.  The forums have always enabled exchange of technical information and exploration of opportunities for collaborations. This was the motivation that led to the convening of the 1st U.S.-Korea Forum on Nanotechnology that was jointly supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation and its Korean counterpart.

Technical Description 
The 19th U.S.-Korea Nanotechnology Forum will bring together a bi-national community of expert researchers and innovators, working on leading-edge, next-generation neuromorphic systems, novel quantum sensing schemes, all based on sustainable semiconductor manufacturing processes. This forum will stimulate efforts to promote these areas.  Expected outcomes of the forum will lead to definition of new milestones and vigorous research collaborative opportunities in both countries, thus advancing investigations of scientific and technological questions with potential to make significant economic development, welfare, and security. The exchange of ideas among leading scientists and engineers in the neuromorphic, quantum sensing, and semiconductor technology areas, will spur new paradigms of investigations in these areas, thus promoting collaborations in them. In addition to individual collaborations, the forum is expected to nurture development new research frameworks by the funding agencies of the two countries. The discussion will enable the U.S. to pivot towards transformative approaches for novel semiconductor manufacturing and sensor development.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
During the past two decades, our annual Forum between the U.S. and Korea in alternating countries has focused on enhancing research collaboration in the field of nanotechnology convergence among scientists and engineers from both countries. Specifically, our joint Forum facilitates networking between the research communities and agencies of both countries, enabling each side to exchange information and explore opportunities for research collaboration. The topics of last year’s 19th Forum were sustainability in semiconductor manufacturing by design and neuromorphic & quantum sensors on a chip. Four keynote speakers, twelve senior presenters, and six early-career presenters from the U.S. were invited, and a roughly equal number of Korean presenters participated. The unique contribution of this Forum is its ability to bring together a bi-national community of expert researchers and innovators who are working on the leading edge of semiconductor manufacturing and advanced sensor technology. The outcome of this Forum has led to groundbreaking milestones and vigorous research collaboration for both countries where semiconductor/sensor technology generate great economic and social impact, which is a focus for both administrations.

As we enter the next industrial revolution, characterized by a convergence of nanotechnology that blurs the lines between the quantum, digital, and biological spheres, the rapid increase in data processed and stored leads us into the emerging field of technologies related to human health and cognition. Specific topics from the 14th and 18th were hybrid bioelectronics and bio-photonics sensors moving to quantum sensors for the enhancement of sensitivity and resolution as well as neuromorphic human sensors on a chip. We further discussed energy efficient and sustainable devices for neuromorphic and quantum applications. We have reexamined topics to promote a paradigm shift for next-generation semiconductor technology, including advanced packaging processes. We further explored sustainability in semiconductor manufacturing including the evaluation of chemistry for materials of high concern, environmental impacts related to future semiconductor fabrication, ultra pure water (UPW) and energy consumption in manufacturing, and novel reduction, reuse, and recycling techniques for UPW in manufacturing. The most important impact and novelty of this Forum was the investigation of sustainability in semiconductor manufacturing by design, which considered alternative materials and processes at the design stage and highlighted modeling to evaluate performance at the microchip. The recovery, reuse, and recycle of E-waste, as well as additive manufacturing of microelectronics, was also examined. We further considered electronics manufacturing for efficient, sustainable, and innovative devices for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and quantum applications.

The format of this Forum consists of keynote speeches, oral presentations, poster presentations, and virtual presentations, as well as subgroup discussions to generate recommendations on the above-mentioned two topics. The discussions will enable the U.S. to pivot towards transformative approaches for novel semiconductor and sensor design and fabrication. We included in this 19th Forum a satellite session of the NanoKorea 2025 Conference to attract a broader audience and maximize impact. In addition, some participants of our Forum presented invited talks at the NanoKorea 2025 Conference.

International collaborative research outcomes can be challenging due to difficulties in identifying mutual benefits as well as sparse funding sources. However, since the 1st U.S.-Korea Nanotechnology Forum, we have promoted and witnessed numerous successful collaborations between the two countries. During the past decade, the Forum participants have created and sustained collaboration teams on topics relevant to both Korea and the U.S. These teams have applied for NSF grants for joint research, and we strongly recommended international collaboration programs between the two countries via this Forum.

All Forum proceedings and findings are available on Carnegie Mellon’s website for a broad audience.

Intellectual Merits

The novel contribution of this Forum is its ability to bring together a bi-national community of expert researchers and innovators who are working on the leading edge of advanced sensor technology, sustainability in semiconductor manufacturing, AI, and quantum technology. This Forum stimulates efforts to promote these areas by utilizing nanotechnology convergence to semiconductor/sensor and environmental technologies. The outcomes of this Forum led to tangible milestones and vigorous research collaboration for both countries where semiconductor/sensor technology significantly impacts national security and economic development.

Broader Impacts

Along with the exchange of ideas among leading scientists and engineers, this Forum recommended new paradigms in semiconductor/sensor technologies. This Forum contributes to national security, the global environment, and economic development via discussions on efficient, sustainable electronics manufacturing and innovative devices for AI and quantum application. This Forum promotes funding opportunities, joint research proposal writing, and research collaboration between the two countries, especially for young scientists.
